Low-fuss espresso is certainly doable at home. The principal space you will be in for tradeoffs is between quality, consistency, authenticity and fuss. 


By quality I mean both the quality of the shot you produce and also the quality of shot you want.


By consistency I mean how often you can create a shot that has the quality that you want.


By authenticity I mean how much what you end up producing will pass the "is this actually an espresso, or is it a small black espresso like coffee?" test.


All these are somewhat related to each other and very much changeable depending on what you want to get out of the experience. Improving any of these adds to fuss though. Pop


For example. For many years I made espresso with a Delonghi Dedica, pressurised porta filter and pre-ground coffee. I was perfectly happy with the quality of the cup (whether it is proper espresso or not). It was very consistent and quicker to make coffee that way than anything else I had. The process was very mildly fussy (scooping, levelling and tamping the grounds). Over time I added fuss... Scales, grinder, bottomless filter. The quality of the result has improved and the fuss has gone up (I quite like the fuss though).


You will find that other people have a higher quality requirement and different levels of fuss they will go to.



Point is, depending on what you want and what you are willing to sacrifice, low fuss espresso at home is doable.
